## Natural history notes

A medium-sized mammal characterized by glossy black fur, bold white stripes running from the head along the back, a bushy tail, and a strong musky defensive spray. In Florida, the Striped Skunk is found in fields, pastures, pine flatwoods, forest edges, hammocks, suburban edges, and open areas with brush piles, logs, burrows, or other sheltered den sites. It is an omnivore that feeds on insects, grubs, small vertebrates, eggs, fruit, carrion, and other foods, mostly foraging at night and relying on its warning coloration and spray to deter predators.
